subject: Re: Unexpected overage in July - ingest window question
messages:
From: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@edgescale.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: billing@edgescale.com
Date: 2026-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected overage in July - ingest window question

Hi Priya,

We pulled our July invoice and saw a ~14% overage relative to our forecast. The usage line that jumped looks tied to a bulk ingest on 2026-07-26 between 23:45 and 00:10 UTC. Our internal logs show a burst of 2.1M events but the sample we attached (edgescale_sample_logs.csv) shows duplicate request_ids for a short window. Can you confirm whether Redwood performs per-request deduplication or if there could be attribution into two billing windows (23:59 -> 00:00 boundary) that would double-count tokens?

We'd like to avoid an invoice hold but need an explanation before we process payment. If this looks like a billing error on Redwood's side we will expect a credit.

Thanks,
Tom Rivera
Director, Platform Engineering
EdgeScale Inc

Attachments: edgescale_sample_logs.csv (CSV, 120KB)
From: priya.natarajan@redwood.com
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@edgescale.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-14T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage in July - ingest window question

Hi Tom — thanks for the note and the sample. We received the file and I’ve looped in Ben (account lead) and Marissa (billing ops).

Quick notes:
- Redwood’s billing pipeline attributes tokens to the ingestion timestamp on our side; we normally dedupe on request_id when possible, but retries that change session attribution or cross a window boundary can surface as additional billable events.
- To help triage we’ll need a short window (approx 23:40–00:15 UTC) of full request_ids + server timestamps — attached sample helped.

Ben — can you confirm contract terms for mid-cycle adjustments for ES-4721?
Marissa — please standby for a request to run a dedupe check and token reconciliation.

Tom — we’ll aim to reply with preliminary findings within 48 hours.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

From: priyom.das@redwood.com
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-15T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected overage in July - ingest window question

Forwarding root-cause analysis from infra team. Short version: during a consumer-side retry storm on 2026-07-26 we briefly saw duplicated request payloads arriving with slightly different session ids; an internal ingestion lag (0–35s) caused some requests to be attributed to the preceding window in our aggregator and others to the following window. Our streaming dedupe uses request_id but only within the same ingestion batch; across out-of-order batches we missed the duplicate link.

Impact estimate: ~7,624 tokens double-counted for the EdgeScale account in that window. We ran a dedupe pass and produced dedup_report_0726.csv.

Proposed remediation:
- Apply a one-time credit for the double-counted token amount ($0.00XX per token, see attached invoice calc)
- Backfill a dedupe rule (cross-batch request_id index) to prevent this recurrence

Marissa, please prepare a credit memo. Ben/Priya, happy to sync if you want more detail.

--
Priyom Das
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

Attachments: dedup_report_0726.csv (CSV, 64KB)
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-17T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage in July - ingest window question

Thanks — I’ve opened BILL-914 and generated an interim credit memo.

Summary:
- Confirmed duped tokens: 7,624 tokens (per priyom’s dedupe pass)
- Credit applied: 7,624 tokens * $0.00095/token = $7.24 (gross) — this will appear as credit line on the August statement; we will reissue an adjusted invoice PDF.
- Invoice to be reissued: 2026-07-31 invoice -> redwood_invoice_adj_0726.pdf attached.

Ben — per the Enterprise SOW we can issue the credit without exec approval (under $10). Please advise if you want the credit held until EdgeScale signs the Q2 renewal addendum.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_invoice_adj_0726.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: priya.natarajan@redwood.com
To: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@edgescale.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage in July - ingest window question

Hi Tom — quick update and confirmation: thanks again for flagging this. Our infra team completed a dedupe pass and we’ve applied a one-time credit of $7.24 to the July invoice; the adjusted invoice (redwood_invoice_adj_0726.pdf) is attached and the credit will be visible on your August statement. We’ve also attached the dedup report (dedup_report_0726.csv) that shows the de-duplicated request ids and token adjustments.

We’ve implemented a cross-batch request_id index in ingestion to prevent cross-window duplication and will monitor the next two billing cycles. If you prefer, we can place a temporary credit hold while you process the adjusted invoice — let me know.

Appreciate you raising this — pleased we could sort quickly.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com
